Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that's all from a contest that turned out to be pretty one-sided, with South Africa levelling the series 1-1. The action now shifts to the scenic hills of Dharamsala, where the 3rd T20I will be played at the HPCA Stadium on 14th December, Sunday. The first ball is at 7 pm (1.30 pm GMT), and as always, we'll be live well before that with all the pre-match build-up. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Quinton de Kock is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his outstanding knock. He says that whenever he gets a start, he tries to convert it. Mentions that he plays against India so much, he gets to score so many runs and the wickets are really good too. Says that Arshdeep Singh has got him out a few times, but he got his tactics right against him in this game. Tells that he felt it was not easy for the new batters, but when India batted, the pitch quickened and made it even tougher for batting.

Aiden Markram, the victorious skipper of South Africa, says it was much better tonight from his side and praises Quinton de Kock for a special knock, adding that the contributions from others in closing out the innings were also important. He feels the bowlers were good in the first game and were even better this evening, which shows that the team is heading in a good direction. The fielding, he says, has also been sharp. Markram notes that there was something in the pitch for the bowlers with the new, hard ball if they hit the right areas. Adds that once you got set, as Quinton de Kock and Tilak Varma showed, it became a lot easier to score. He calls it a great stadium and says it was a really enjoyable game to be part of. Speaking about squad rotation, he admits it’s never easy for players, but the priority is to identify the best XI for the World Cup. He stresses the importance of putting your hand up when the team needs it. Further says that you are never bigger than the team and believes this is a trait carried by others in the squad as well. He finishes by saying he would have liked to maximise his balls a bit better today.

Suryakumar Yadav, the captain of India, says that they bowled first but couldn't do much at the start. However, they came back well and it is all about learning. Mentions that dew did play a factor but they also should have changed plans when things didn't go their way. Says that he and Shubman Gill need to take more responsibility as they can't always rely on Abhishek Sharma. Ends by saying that Axar Patel was the better choice at 3 for this game, but they will see how things go in the upcoming games.
Presentation Time ...

Ottneil Baartman is up for a quick chat. He says there was nothing too fancy about his approach today. Explains that the two frontline seamers set the tone beautifully upfront, which allowed him to come into the game with clarity. He adds that while Marco Jansen and Lungi Ngidi looked for swing early on, he and Lutho Sipamla are more 'hit-the-wicket' bowlers, so they focused on varying seam positions to make the most of a surface that tended to skid on. Baartman emphasises that T20 cricket moves quickly, and as a bowler, you need to be ready the moment the captain turns to you. Ends by acknowledging that when a team is three or four down inside the Powerplay, it becomes very difficult to get across the line, and credits Jansen and Ngidi for the damage they inflicted upfront.

South Africa will be more than satisfied with their bowling effort. They knew early wickets would be vital, and Marco Jansen and Lungi Ngidi delivered two gems to remove the Indian openers. Jansen piled on the pressure by dismissing the opposition skipper as well, giving his side firm control of the game. They never really allowed the hosts back in, even with Tilak Varma playing a fine hand. George Linde kept things tight, while Lutho Sipamla chipped in with a couple of wickets. And it only got better as Ottneil Baartman picked up three in the penultimate over to complete a brilliant four-fer, before Lungi Ngidi applied the finishing touch to wrap things up.

Earlier in the game, South Africa piled up a massive total that included 15 towering sixes. Quinton de Kock set the tone with a fluent 46-ball 90, while David Miller and Donovan Ferreira unleashed a fiery 53-run stand off just 23 deliveries to close things out. Varun Chakaravarthy was the standout bowler for India with a couple of wickets, and Axar Patel added one more, but beyond that, it was a disappointing outing. The frontline seamers, Arshdeep Singh and Jasprit Bumrah, took some serious punishment and went for plenty of runs.

Tilak Varma was the only one who looked in complete control, refusing to rush like the others. He showcased a wide range of strokes and brought up his 5th T20I fifty, but Hardik Pandya struggled for timing and never quite resembled the batter who rescued India in the first game. Jitesh Sharma walked in and struck a few lusty blows, but by then the asking rate had shot past 15 rpo, and under mounting pressure, he too fell. Tilak kept going in his own rhythm, but with little to no support, it turned into a Herculean task for him alone as the hosts eventually fell well short.

India needed a flying start in their chase, but things went the other way as Shubman Gill fell for a golden duck, extending his lean patch, while SKY once again couldn’t make much of an impact. Abhishek Sharma got a start but couldn’t carry on either, leaving the hosts three down inside the Powerplay and immediately on the back foot. Axar Patel's promotion didn’t click, and just when he and Tilak Varma began to stitch together a partnership, Axar fell, leaving India wobbling at 67/4.

South Africa level the series with a commanding win! These two sides just keep trading blows on this tour, with neither willing to let the other pull away, making the contest all the more exciting and entertaining. After going down in the first game, the Proteas have bounced back in style here, completely outplaying the hosts in every facet of the game. This also marks India's second-biggest defeat in terms of runs in this format, and with this result, South Africa become the most successful side against the hosts in T20Is

OUT! CAUGHT! A fine low grab from Reeza Hendricks and South Africa break through just as India seemed to be gaining a bit of momentum. Fuller and going across the left-hander, Axar stays leg side of the ball and looks to thrash it through the off side. Neither does he manage to keep it along the ground nor pick the gap. Hits it uppishly and straight to cover, where Reeza Hendricks gets low and has his hands out in front with his body weight going backwards. The third umpire is called into action. After zooming in on one of the angles, the third umpire is happy that Reeza has his fingers under the ball. Axar's promotion to number 3 does not work out the way India had hoped. He falls for a run-a-ball 21. India are now 67/4.
Commentary.Howout: c Reeza Hendricks b Ottneil Baartman
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.3: Ottneil Baartman to Axar Patel, OUT! c Reeza Hendricks b Ottneil Baartman.

Commentary.Commentary: Has that carried? Reeza Hendricks is not sure, and the third umpire has been called in to check the legality of the catch. After a few replays from different angles, it has been deemed a fair grab.
Goes into the surface again, outside off, Varma takes a step across and drags the pull to long on for one more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.2: Ottneil Baartman to Tilak Varma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a hard length, over off, Axar swivels for the pull but gets an inside edge down to deep fine leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 7.1: Ottneil Baartman to Axar Patel, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Double change. Ottneil Baartman replaces Marco Jansen.

Two is the call and they get it! Drops it short and quick, on middle and leg, Tilak tucks it with soft hands in the vacant mid-wicket region. Donovan Ferreira thought about going after it but then bailed out. Dewald Brevis charges in and gets rid of the ball but cannot prevent Axar from completing the second run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.6: Donovan Ferreira to Tilak Varma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: This is slowed down, on the fuller side, Varma lunges and eases it in front of point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.5: Donovan Ferreira to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! In the gap! Pushed through by Donovan, shorter and quicker, on middle. Tilak Varma backs away to pick his spot. Cuts it to the right of deep point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Donovan Ferreira to Tilak Varma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Short and at the pads, Patel nurdles it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Donovan Ferreira to Axar Patel, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! In the arc and Axar Patel goes big! Sliding on with the arm, fuller and on off. Axar frees his arms and launches it over long on for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Donovan Ferreira to Axar Patel, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Darted in from around the wicket, short and on middle. Tilak punches it to long off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Donovan Ferreira to Tilak Varma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Donovan Ferreira comes into the attack right after the Powerplay.

Fuller and in the channel, Axar steers it straight to short third. Not much seperating the two sides in terms of the runs at this stage as South Africa scored 53 runs in the Powerplay but India have lost a couple of wickets more than the tourists.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Marco Jansen to Axar Patel, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: This is on a hard length, around off, nips away off the deck. Tilak looks to get behind the line and keep it out with a straight bat. Gets squared up as the ball goes off the outer half behind point for one more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Marco Jansen to Tilak Varma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pace taken off and into the surface, outside off, Axar stays leg side of the ball and swings a bit too hard. Loses his shape in the process and drags it towards mid on for one. 50 up for India!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Marco Jansen to Axar Patel, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Lands it on a short of a length, outside off, Patel swings at it and slices it off the bottom half of the bat. Gets enough bat on it to clear mid off. Aiden Markram gives it a chase and hauls it in with a slide. Two runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Marco Jansen to Axar Patel, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: On a hard length, on off, Varma rides the bounce and drops it in front of short third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Marco Jansen to Tilak Varma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Risky single! Short and wide on off, Axar flat bats it in front of mid off and starts running as soon as he hits it. It goes straight to Aiden Markram, who picks it up cleanly and has a shy at the bowling end but misses. Axar was gone had the throw hit.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Marco Jansen to Axar Patel, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on leg, Tilak Varma glances it towards deep fine leg for a couple of runs. 13 runs off Sipamla's first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Lutho Sipamla to Tilak Varma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Even better now! Back of a length but around the leg stump line. Tilak Varma gets inside the line of it and helps it on its way over the deep fine leg fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Lutho Sipamla to Tilak Varma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Gets it away! Fuller delivery and around off. Tilak Varma uses his feet, stays leg side of the ball and thumps it to the right of mid off for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Lutho Sipamla to Tilak Varma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length and outside off, Axar Patel backs away and cuts it to deep point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Lutho Sipamla to Axar Patel, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on middle, Axar Patel pats it towards mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Lutho Sipamla to Axar Patel, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and on middle, Axar Patel knocks it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Lutho Sipamla to Axar Patel, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on middle, Tilak Varma blocks it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Marco Jansen to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tilak Varma is in at number 5.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Excellent review from South Africa, and Marco Jansen gets his second. This is on a hard length and around off, shaping away. Suryakumar Yadav has a poke at it but misses as the ball goes past the outside edge behind, where QDK dives to his right to grab it. There is a noise, and Marco Jansen appeals for a caught behind, but it is turned down. Jansen looks the most interested, but Quinton de Kock is not sure. However, after a long conversation with the keeper and the bowler, Aiden Markram goes upstairs with 3 seconds to go. UltraEdge comes up and shows a big spike when the ball passes the bat. SKY starts to walk off. India are 32/3, and in a spot of bother.
Commentary.Howout: c Quinton de Kock b Marco Jansen
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Marco Jansen to Suryakumar Yadav, OUT! c Quinton de Kock b Marco Jansen.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched up and on off, Suryakumar Yadav drives it wide of cover, where Dewald Brevis dives to his right to make a fine stop.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Marco Jansen to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on middle, Axar Patel knocks it towards mid on for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Marco Jansen to Axar Patel, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on off, Suryakumar Yadav steers it through point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Marco Jansen to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Beautiful shot! Full again and around off. Suryakumar Yadav gets his hands through the shot. He opens the face of his bat and caresses it through covers for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Marco Jansen to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Fuller but way outside off, Suryakumar Yadav leaves it alone. Wided.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Marco Jansen to Suryakumar Yadav, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Up and over! Pitched up and just outside off. Axar Patel gets the chance to free his arms and lofts it over extra cover for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Lungi Ngidi to Axar Patel, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Touch fuller, on middle and off, Axar Patel uses his feet to slog it across the line but loses his shape and bunts it back towards the bowler. Ngidi dives to his right to make the stop on the followthrough.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Lungi Ngidi to Axar Patel, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bangs this into the pitch, outside off, Axar Patel chases after it, but gets a bottom edge that beats the keeper to his left and goes behind. Two taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Lungi Ngidi to Axar Patel, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length and on off, Axar Patel mistimes his cut towards cover. Three dots in a row.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Lungi Ngidi to Axar Patel, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and around off, Axar Patel stabs it out to extra cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Lungi Ngidi to Axar Patel, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length and outside off, angling away, Axar Patel tries to cut it away but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Lungi Ngidi to Axar Patel, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: India's skipper, Suryakumar Yadav comes out to bat.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Marco Jansen with an absolute peach of a delivery. He hits the length hard and on middle, threatens to angle in but shapes away after hitting the deck. Abhishek Sharma stays back to defend, but just like Gill, gets opened up as he plays for the angle. It takes the outside edge and goes behind, where Quinton de Kock makes no mistake. Jansen loved that dismissal, and it is a big one for South Africa as well. Abhishek departs for 17 off 8, and India are 19/2, having lost both the openers.
Commentary.Howout: c Quinton de Kock b Marco Jansen
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, OUT! c Quinton de Kock b Marco Jansen.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length and outside off, Abhishek Sharma looks to slap it away but gets it from the toe-end of the bat. It flies over extra cover but slows down in the outfield. Two taken. The umpire checks for a short run, and the replay shows that Abhishek just about gets his bat over the line at the other end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length and around off, Axar Patel runs it down to deep third man for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Marco Jansen to Axar Patel, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: BEATEN! Goes fuller and on middle, angles in and then shapes away. Axar Patel looks to clip it across the line but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Marco Jansen to Axar Patel, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Marco Jansen sees the batter back away and serves this full, outside off, gets it to shape away. Abhishek Sharma is too far away from the ball and fails to reach it. It keeps on moving away behind the stumps as QDK only manages to parry it to his left. A bye taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, Bye.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BOOM! Welcome to the game, Marco Jansen. He lands this on a back of a length and around off, sits up nicely for the batter. Abhishek Sharma stands tall and pulls it with disdain over the deep square leg fence for another biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Who will bowl from the other end? It will be Marco Jansen.

Big swing and a miss! Lungi Ngidi bangs this into the pitch and just on off, Axar Patel looks to pull it away but goes a bit too hard. Loses his shape and misses. 9 runs and a wicket from the first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Lungi Ngidi to Axar Patel, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Axar Patel is in at number 3.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! Lungi Ngidi draws first blood, and Shubman Gill's miserable run continues. Ngidi lands this on a good length and around the fourth stump line. Gets it to shape away from the batter and late too. Gill stays back to play at it but gets squared up completely with the movement. It takes the outside edge and flies fast to the right of first slip, where Reeza Hendricks moves to that side to take a sharp catch. Gill goes back for a golden duck, and India are 9/1, chasing 214 runs.
Commentary.Howout: c Reeza Hendricks b Lungi Ngidi
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Lungi Ngidi to Shubman Gill, OUT! c Reeza Hendricks b Lungi Ngidi.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length and on middle, nips back in a bit, Abhishek Sharma swipes it off the inside half of the bat to deep square leg for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BANG! Did not take long for Abhishek Sharma to go big. This is fuller and just outside off. Sharma extends his arms to reach out for it and carves it over the deep extra cover fence for the first biggie of the chase.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on off, moves away from the left-hander. Abhishek Sharma stays back and tries to heave it across the line but gets a bottom edge on the bounce to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Intent right away from Abhishek Sharma! Lungi Ngidi starts with a good-length delivery, on middle, angling away. Abhishek uses his feet to pull it away but gets an inside edge through square leg for a couple of runs. India are up and running in the chase!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, 2 runs.
